summaryPoints: India built a commanding first-innings platform of 502/7, spearheaded by MA Agarwal's brilliant 215.
South Africa replied strongly with 431, powered by Dean Elgar's commanding century (160) to swing the contest.
A ruthless second-innings declaration at 323/4d by India established a massive 395 Runs target.
Mohammed Shami spearheaded India's attack to bowl out South Africa for 191 and seal victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Dr. Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as India posted 502/7 (135.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, South Africa countered with 431/10 (131.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 7-Wicket Spell: R Ashwin (7/145), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Rohit Sharma delivered a masterclass for India (303 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 53%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, South Africa faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by MA Agarwal (222 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by 203 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While South Africa produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
